correctness.rationale: For ψ(z)=-log(1-z) and normalized Szego kernels, disk automorphism ψ(φ_w(z))-ψ(w)=log(1-conj(w)z)-log(1+ηz) (|η|=1) gives exact Fourier coefficients ((-η)^n-conj(w)^n)/n. Parseval gives Φ(w)=π²/6+Li₂(|w|²)-2Re Li₂(-ηw). Angular monotonicity bounds Φ(w)≤π²/6+2Li₂(|w|), with equality for real positive w and limit π²/2. Separately Schur with p_j=(j+1/2)^(-1/2), convex midpoint quadrature and beta integral bounds Hilbert-matrix norm by π; log-block positive Rayleigh vectors give limiting lower bound π. The Bonsall identity equates kernel variance to testing norm. Positive-definite moment Gram blocks of arbitrarily large size prove infinite rank. All quantifiers over w in disk, not just tested sample points; finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: A canonical unbounded BMOA function generates the classical infinite-rank Hilbert Hankel matrix. Its exact Garsia/kernel-testing norm is a naturally motivated and separately computable invariant compared with the full operator norm; the ratio 1/sqrt2 quantitatively exhibits failure of the SRKT precisely in the 2026 unbounded-symbol research context. This is a useful sharp-for-the-symbol benchmark, not merely a routine relabeling, and neither claims a universal separation nor resolves existence of positive unbounded SRKT symbols.
